subject.title: [Bug]: Agent reads workspace files after tool discovery, causing timeouts on natural language queries

question: For slow local-model backends, should OpenClaw change first-turn behavior so injected workspace guidance can take precedence over Tool Search discovery, or should the current Tool Search-first lean-mode contract remain with documented opt-outs?
rationale: Current source already injects workspace files, but the docs deliberately treat TOOLS.md as guidance rather than availability; changing that precedence is a product/tool-policy decision with prompt-size and discoverability tradeoffs.

options.title: Define an opt-in slow-backend policy
options.body: Add or document a narrow opt-in path that makes first-turn workspace guidance win over Tool Search for proven slow local backends, with live repro and regression coverage before changing runtime behavior.

options.title: Keep the current lean-mode contract
options.body: Leave Tool Search defaults intact and direct affected users to explicit configuration such as disabling or tuning Tool Search for local backends.

options.title: Fold into broader prompt-context work
options.body: Track this as part of the broader smaller-model prompt/context and workspace capability convention issues before accepting a narrow runtime policy change.

recommendation.title: Define an opt-in slow-backend policy
recommendation.body: Add or document a narrow opt-in path that makes first-turn workspace guidance win over Tool Search for proven slow local backends, with live repro and regression coverage before changing runtime behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent local-model lean and embedded-runner work makes vincentkoc the best current routing candidate for the policy choice.
